paper_title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image. Visual token pruning methods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore propose LOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, so LOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average. LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/

Introduction Recent diffusion language models match similarly sized autoregressive models while refining several masked positions in parallel over denoising steps (Nie et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2025a). In diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) such as LLaDA-V (You et al., 2026) and others (Yang et al., 2025a; Yu et al., 2025), bidirectional attention prevents direct use of the exact key-value caching found in autoregressive models, so standard inference processes the full multimodal sequence at every step. Visual tokens dominate this sequence, accounting for 8997% of LLaDA-Vs input across our benchmarks (Figure 1b), while forward without them costs only 310% as much. DVLM decoding therefore spends most of its compute repeatedly processing an unchanged visual input. Existing methods reduce this cost through visual token pruning (Chang et al., 2026; Xu et al., 2026; Kim et al., 2026) (Figure 1a), intermediate-state caching (Wu et al., 2026a; Liu et al., 2026; Nguyen-Tri et al., 2026), or unmasking more tokens per step (Kim et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026b; Wu et al., 2026b; Wang et al., 2026; Lee et al., 2026). These approaches make image-conditioned forwards cheaper, reuse their computation, or run fewer decoding steps, but none asks whether the current step needs the image. We ask whether removing the image would change the models decision at the current decoding state. Comparing LLaDA-Vs predictions with and without the image along the same decoding trajectory reveals substantial redundancy (Section 3.2). The two give the same top-1 token at 83.4% of the positions selected for unmasking, and 85.0% of final tokens had already appeared as top-1 predictions before unmasking. Within trajectory, image-dependent steps tend to cluster early rather than recur periodically, while their overall share varies from 7.9% on MMBench to 43.8% on DocVQA. fixed schedule therefore finds it hard to capture when the image is needed. These observations motivate deciding image access per input and step from predictions the model has already computed. We propose LOWN (Look Only When Needed), decoding method built on this redundancy. LOWN stores the top-1 predictions and confidences from the latest image-conditioned forward, which we call the FULL forward, as an anchor and tests it with cheap TEXT-ONLY forward at each step. LOWN requires neither training nor task-specific threshold and can be added to visual token pruning or key-value caching because it reduces how often FULL forward is needed (Figure 1b). The same rule transfers to LaViDa and VidLaDA. Our contributions are as follows. We show through paired FULL and TEXT-ONLY forward comparisons that most DVLM decoding steps can skip image access, while the necessary steps vary across trajectories and are not well captured by fixed schedules. We introduce LOWN, training-free and threshold-free method that uses prediction agreement to jointly decide when to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. We validate LOWN across ten benchmarks and three DVLM backbones, retaining 99.6% of LLaDA-Vs score at 0.35 its decoding FLOPs, composing orthogonally with visual token pruning, and running under key-value caching. 2 Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs 2. Related Work Diffusion language and vision-language models. Discrete diffusion and masked diffusion models generate sequences through iterative token recovery (Austin et al., 2021; Sahoo et al., 2024; Shi et al., 2024). This paradigm has scaled to large language models (Nie et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2025a) and extended to image and video understanding (DiffusionGemma Team, 2026; You et al., 2026; Li et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2025; He et al., 2026). These models establish the DVLM setting studied here. LOWN addresses the complementary inference question of how often denoising must reprocess the visual input. Efficient inference for diffusion LMs and VLMs. Visual-token reduction shortens the visual sequence in vision transformers and autoregressive VLMs (Bolya et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2025; Xing et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025b). ZOO-Prune (Kim et al., 2026) combines projector-level sensitivity estimates with diversity-aware selection. For diffusion VLMs, RedVTP prunes using attention from still-masked response tokens, while D3ToM uses previously decoded tokens to guide visual-token selection and merging (Xu et al., 2026; Chang et al., 2026). These methods determine which visual tokens forward processes, but they lose the removed information (Endo et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026a). Other work keeps the visual input and reduces the number of steps or the cost of forward. Decoding schedules unmask multiple tokens per step when confidence, cross-step stability, or attention to the image supports it (Wei et al., 2026; Wu et al., 2026a; Yu et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2026b; Wang et al., 2026; Lee et al., 2026). Prophet (Li et al., 2026b) unmasks all remaining tokens once the average top-two logit gap in the answer region is large enough. KLASS (Kim et al., 2025) combines confidence with cross-step distribution stability and is our schedule baseline. Caching methods reuse intermediate states across denoising steps (Ma et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2026; Nguyen-Tri et al., 2026; Li et al., 2025), and we compose LOWN with Fast-dLLM (Wu et al., 2026a), blockwise approximate key-value cache. Pruning and caching act inside forward, on the tokens it processes or the states it reuses, and schedules on how many tokens step unmasks. LOWN decides both whether step processes the image and how many tokens it unmasks from the agreement between TEXT-ONLY and the last image-conditioned prediction, and, keeping only predictions, it runs on top of pruning and caching. 3. Method LOWN separates two decisions that standard DVLM decoding makes with single FULL forward, whether the current response state needs the image and how far decoding can advance (Figure 3). It retains the last image-conditioned prediction as an anchor, tests that anchor with TEXT-ONLY forward, and runs FULL forward only when the test cannot certify enough tokens. B. Method Details and Cost Accounting This appendix gives the complete decoding procedure, restates the cost model of Section 4.3 and derives its forward cost 𝒞(𝑛), and writes visual token pruning in the same form as Equation 3. B.1. Detailed Decoding Algorithm Each response starts fully masked, with its length and baseline unmasking schedule set by the benchmark protocol. The first iteration runs TEXT-ONLY followed by FULL on the same response, establishing the anchor and unmasking 𝑘 positions. Confidence is the softmax probability of the top-1 token. The repetition guard ends the certified prefix before candidate whose token ID matches either immediate neighbor that is already unmasked or was accepted earlier in the same scan. The guard is needed because the positions accepted on one TEXT-ONLY step are predicted independently of one another, so two adjacent positions can receive the same token, and without the guard such pairs would be unmasked together and appear as repeated words in the response. Algorithm 1 gives the full procedure. B.2. Cost of One Forward Section 4.3 writes the cost of LOWN relative to the baseline as 𝑅 = 𝑓 + 𝜎𝜌 (Equation 3). The baseline runs 𝑇 FULL forwards over 𝑁𝐹 = 𝑣+𝑐+𝑥𝑡 tokens.
